owner_and_source: Federal Transit Administration (FTA), National Transit Database -- 'Complete Monthly Ridership (with Adjustments and Estimates)', dataset 8bui-9xvu on the USDOT open-data portal data.transportation.gov. No API key, no registration.
license_and_commercial_rights: Public Domain U.S. Government (the portal's own machine-readable licence field is licenseId=USGOV_WORKS, name='Public Domain U.S. Government', termsLink https://www.usa.gov/government-works, and the dataset's DCAT Common Core License field is http://www.usa.gov/publicdomain/label/1.0/). A work of the United States federal government, not subject to domestic copyright (17 U.S.C. Sec. 105). COMMERCIAL USE IS PERMITTED without restriction, licence fee, or attribution obligation; crediting FTA/NTD is customary courtesy, not a licence condition. No share-alike, no field-of-use limitation, no revocation clause -- unlike the per-agency GTFS developer licence agreements surveyed in data/acquired/US_OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md.
geography: United States, nationwide -- all NTD-reporting transit agencies (~1,900 reporters) across all 50 states, DC and the territories
time_coverage: monthly, January 2002 to the most recent published month (rolling; the portal refreshes monthly, R/P1M)
schema_and_format: CSV, ~368,900 data rows x ~20 columns. One row per agency x mode x type-of-service x month, carrying Unlinked Passenger Trips (UPT), Vehicle Revenue Miles (VRM), Vehicle Revenue Hours (VRH) and Vehicles Operated in Max Service (VOMS), plus NTD ID, agency name, UZA/UACE, mode and TOS codes. This is the SAME dataset data/curated/fetch_ntd_monthly.py already pulls, but UNFILTERED: the repo currently retains only the DR/DT (demand-response) slice in data/curated/panels/ntd_monthly_dr.csv.gz. The full table adds every fixed-route mode -- MB (bus), CB (commuter bus), RB (bus rapid transit), HR/LR/CR (rail), VP (vanpool), FB (ferry) and the rest.
update_frequency: monthly (portal Update Frequency R/P1M). source_checksum is null: the table grows by one month each release, so the sha256 recorded at acquisition is provenance for THIS vintage, not a reproducibility guarantee.
canonical_contract: none-yet -- an aggregate agency-mode-month demand panel. It is training and backtest input to the Program E forecasters that emit themis.canonical.entities.ForecastVintage; it is not itself an instance of any canonical entity, because Milexium's canonical model is trip-level (ServiceRequest / Outcome / VehicleObservation) and has no aggregate-ridership entity today. That gap is real and is recorded here rather than papered over.

quality_tests.name: header_has_upt_and_ntd_id
quality_tests.description: first line contains an NTD ID column and an unlinked-passenger-trips (UPT) column -- proves the export is the ridership table, not a Socrata error page

quality_tests.name: row_count_exceeds_dr_only_slice
quality_tests.description: more than 300,000 data rows, i.e. materially broader than the demand-response-only slice already retained in data/curated/panels/

quality_tests.name: covers_multiple_modes
quality_tests.description: the mode column contains fixed-route modes (MB and/or CB/RB/HR/LR) and not only DR/DT

acceptance_threshold: downloads, is CSV, > 40 MB, > 300,000 data rows, and the mode column spans more than the two demand-response codes. A truncated Socrata response (the API silently pages at 1,000 rows if the wrong endpoint is used) would fail all three.
retention_and_deletion: retain: this is the demand-model breadth corpus and the direct evidence behind data/curated/TRANSFER_RESULTS.md's cross-city pretraining result. Cheaply reproducible from the portal, so evictable ahead of contractual/audit records, but re-pulling gives a DIFFERENT vintage (one more month), so the retained object is the reproducible reference for any backtest that cites it.
